clue.text: A gaol to make the hair stand on end

definitions.meaning: a cell or small jail where someone is locked in

definitions.text: make the hair stand on end
definitions.meaning: read literally, to set a lock of hair pointing upwards

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is playful: a lock is a strand of hair, so making it stand is putting a lock up.
explanation.definitionFit: A gaol is a lock-up, and making a lock of hair stand up is to 'lock up' read as a phrase.

clue.text: Call for retirement from most recent job

parts.note: the last one is the most recent
a post is a job or position

explanation.surface: A summons to retire comes from someone's latest job.
explanation.walkthrough: The Last Post is a bugle call sounded at night to signal soldiers to turn in.
explanation.definitionFit: This bugle call signals soldiers to bed, the night's retirement, and is played at funerals.

clue.text: Firm kiss planted on crest of peacock

indicators.note: in a down clue the first pieces sit on top of the next

parts.note: Co is short for company, a firm
X is the sign for a kiss
a comb is the fleshy crest on a bird's head

explanation.surface: A firm kiss lands on the crest of a peacock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peacock' looks like the bird with a crest, but it is the definition: a vain dandy.
explanation.definitionFit: A coxcomb is a vain show-off, just as a peacock describes a strutting dandy.

clue.text: Leave Suffolk free from draught?

parts.note: a Suffolk Punch is a draught horse; freeing it from pulling means taking off its tack

explanation.walkthrough: Suffolk suggests the English county; it is the Suffolk Punch, a heavy farm horse, and draught is pulling, not cold air.
explanation.definitionFit: To unharness a horse is to remove its tack and release it from pulling a load.

clue.text: After thought, get together to adapt unknown instrument

indicators.note: the pieces are told to come together, so they are joined end to end

parts.note: an afterthought added to a letter is a PS, a postscript
to adapt something is to alter it
Y is an algebraic unknown, like X and Z

explanation.surface: Someone, after reflection, gathers to adapt a strange musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After thought' reads as 'after thinking', but run together it is an afterthought, a PS.
explanation.definitionFit: A psaltery is an ancient stringed instrument plucked with the fingers, so it is a kind of musical instrument.

clue.text: How the nurseryman behaved when approaching the fair?

definitions.text: How the nurseryman behaved when approaching the fair?

parts.words: How the nurseryman behaved when approaching the fair?
parts.note: the nursery-rhyme simpleton met a pieman going to the fair

explanation.walkthrough: 'nurseryman' suggests a plant grower; it is the man of the nursery rhyme Simple Simon, who met a pieman going to the fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting simply and foolishly is behaving in a naive, dim manner, as Simple Simon did.

clue.text: Call a priest — a woolly-haired one!

indicators.note: to call a word is to say it, so it is heard rather than written

parts.note: a lama is a Tibetan Buddhist priest

explanation.surface: Summon a cleric, a shaggy-haired one at that.
explanation.definitionFit: The llama is a South American animal with a thick woolly coat.

clue.text: Caught out finally after single, resulting in draw

indicators.note: after places the caught and final pieces behind the first word

parts.note: a single extra is one, such as a single person hired in a crowd scene
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: finally takes the closing letter of the word out

explanation.surface: A batter is caught after taking a single, and the match ends in a draw.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket words mislead: 'draw' is not a tied match but to pull out.
explanation.definitionFit: To extract a tooth is to draw it, pulling something out.

clue.text: Some way off? Could be done within the year

indicators.note: within puts the reworked letters inside the year
could be signals another possible arrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: Is it far away? It could be done inside a year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Could be' signals the anagram of the four-letter word, and 'within' sets it inside the abbreviated year.
explanation.definitionFit: Yonder means over there, at a distance.

clue.text: In charge on river he may check you in and out?

definitions.text: he may check you in and out

parts.note: a commission is a charge or authority to act
the Aire is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: Someone in charge by a river may log your arrival and departure.
explanation.walkthrough: A commissionaire is a uniformed doorman at a hotel or cinema.
explanation.definitionFit: A uniformed doorkeeper greets guests arriving and leaving a hotel or office.

clue.text: Vi details the essential nature of the upper class

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals

indicators.note: to de-tail a word is to cut off its tail, its final letter

parts.note: form can mean the essential nature or shape of a thing

explanation.surface: A woman called Vi describes the essence of the upper classes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'details' is read as de-tails: THE loses its last letter to give TH. A sixth form is the top class in a British secondary school, for students aged 16 to 18.
explanation.definitionFit: In British schools the sixth form is the senior year group, the highest class in the building.

clue.text: Jacket bearing a Bronte name

definitions.meaning: an old padded quilted jacket worn under armour, also spelt aketon
Anne Bronte published under the pen-name ... Bell

explanation.definitionFit: An acton was a padded jerkin worn beneath mail, and Acton Bell was the pseudonym used by Anne Bronte.

clue.text: American plan giving weight to paid performer

parts.note: a pro is a professional, someone paid to perform
a gram is a small unit of weight

explanation.surface: An American scheme to add weight to a professional entertainer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'giving weight to' adds the weight after the performer; the answer is the American spelling of the British programme.
explanation.definitionFit: A programme is a plan or schedule, and the shorter spelling is the US form.

clue.text: Giving away sound vegetable coming to maturity

indicators.note: sound tells us the vegetable is heard, not spelt

parts.note: a leek is an onion-like vegetable
to come of age is to reach maturity

explanation.surface: A healthy vegetable is given away as it ripens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like an adjective, healthy, describing the vegetable; it is the homophone signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Leakage is the disclosure of secrets, so it is a giving away of information.

clue.text: Black paintbrush

definitions.meaning: an artist's brush made from the fur of the marten-like animal

explanation.definitionFit: Sable is the heraldic tincture for black, and fine artists' brushes are made from sable hair.

clue.text: Put on mule I sat awkwardly

indicators.note: awkwardly suggests the letters of these words are clumsily rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone climbs clumsily onto a mule and sits there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put on' looks physical, like donning a slipper (a mule), but it means fake.
explanation.definitionFit: To put on an accent or a feeling is to fake or imitate it.

clue.text: Person unlikely to break the ice

definitions.text: Person unlikely to break the ice

parts.words: Person unlikely to break the ice
parts.note: breaking the ice starts a party's conversation, which needs someone there at the start

explanation.walkthrough: Breaking the ice is starting conversation among strangers; someone who turns up late misses that moment.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who arrives after the others has missed the start where icebreaking happens.

clue.text: Took an internal flight from the ground

definitions.text: Took an internal flight from the ground

parts.words: Took an internal flight from the ground
parts.note: a flight of stairs inside a house, climbed from the ground floor

explanation.walkthrough: An internal flight sounds like a domestic plane trip; it is a flight of stairs.
explanation.definitionFit: To climb the stairs from the ground floor is to go up or rise.

clue.text: Unrest in Spain following article is dramatic

indicators.note: following places the reworked letters after the article

parts.note: the is the definite article

indicators.note: unrest in the country means its letters are in turmoil and rearranged

explanation.surface: A news report on Spanish unrest after an article is described as dramatic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unrest in' scrambles the country's letters; 'following' puts them after the article. 'dramatic' here means to do with drama, not exciting.
explanation.definitionFit: Thespian is an adjective for anything to do with acting and the theatre.

clue.text: Frustrate purpose of guillotine?

definitions.meaning: a guillotine is designed to cut the top of a person away

explanation.definitionFit: To head someone off is to block or intercept them, and a guillotine's job is literally to take the head off.

clue.text: The Gentlemen — a cricket side in the heartless twenties

indicators.note: in places the cricket side inside the remaining letters
heartless removes the whole middle of the word, leaving only its first and last letters

parts.note: the off side is one half of a cricket field

explanation.surface: An old cricket team called the Gentlemen played in the uncaring 1920s.
explanation.walkthrough: Gentlemen v Players was an old cricket fixture of amateurs against professionals. TOFFS is British slang for upper-class people.
explanation.definitionFit: Toffs are well-to-do upper-class men, the type once called gentlemen.

clue.text: Bit of skirt having a fling

definitions.meaning: a frill sewn onto a skirt
throwing oneself about in an angry, showy way

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bit of skirt' is slang for a woman and 'having a fling' an affair, but both are literal.
explanation.definitionFit: A flounce is a ruffled strip on a skirt, and to flounce is to fling oneself about in temper.

clue.text: Check with alternative leader

parts.note: to edit copy is to check it
or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: Someone checks with the alternative leader.
explanation.walkthrough: On a newspaper the editor is its head, and leaders, or editorials, are the editor's columns.
explanation.definitionFit: The editor heads a newspaper's staff and is its chief.

clue.text: Force to be a soldier

definitions.meaning: to coerce or bully someone into doing something
a mounted infantryman of former times

explanation.definitionFit: To dragoon someone is to coerce them, and a dragoon was a cavalryman carrying a musket.

clue.text: His deeds should justify his status

definitions.text: His deeds should justify his status

parts.words: His deeds should justify his status
parts.note: deeds here are title deeds to property, not actions

explanation.walkthrough: 'deeds' suggests actions, but title deeds are the legal papers proving who holds a property.
explanation.definitionFit: A property holder proves possession through the title deeds in their name.

clue.text: Fence round the quarters and shut down

parts.note: east and north are quarters of the compass, E and N
to close a shop is to shut it down

explanation.surface: Fence in the living quarters and shut the place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the quarters' looks like living quarters but means compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: To enclose a field is to surround it with a fence or wall.

clue.text: Sharp spine removes hummingbird's beak

indicators.note: removes says the beak is taken away from the bird's name

parts.note: the thornbill is a kind of hummingbird
a bird's beak is its bill

explanation.surface: A sharp spine strips a hummingbird of its beak.
explanation.definitionFit: A thorn is a sharp spike on a stem, like a prickle on a rose.

clue.text: New model line doomed to failure

indicators.note: new indicates the letters take a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A new product line is destined to flop.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ill-omened has bad signs over it from the start, so it seems fated to fail.

clue.text: Whistler fell and was sent to a specialist

parts.note: a referee, the ref, blows a whistle
to fall from grace is to sin, to have erred

explanation.surface: A whistler tripped over and was passed on to a consultant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whistler' suggests the painter, but it is the match official.
explanation.definitionFit: A patient referred by a GP has been passed on to a hospital consultant.

clue.text: A familiar close to the day

parts.note: Fri is short for Friday
the close of something is its end

explanation.surface: A friend arrives at the end of the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'familiar' reads as an adjective but is a noun, an intimate companion.
explanation.definitionFit: A familiar is a close companion or intimate acquaintance.
